answer.exemplar: Evidence is bought in proportion to what being wrong costs, so a choice that can be undone in a day needs only enough reading to rule out something absurd, while a choice that cannot be undone needs the comparison, the measurement and the review. This is not a licence to be careless: the cheap-to-reverse choice still needs a written reason, because in a year nobody will remember why the obvious option was passed over. The common failure is to spend the effort belonging to the irreversible decision on the reversible one, arriving at a beautifully documented choice that is cheap to undo and a perfunctory one that cannot be. Deciding by reversibility also makes the two kinds legible: a list of what is cheap to change, and a short list of what needs a day of real work before it is made.

answer.exemplar: A decision can be wrong on the technical merits and still right, because the alternative carries a cost larger than the problem being solved: a fortnight of delay is cheaper than a quarter of engineering time. What makes that defensible rather than merely convenient is the measurement, since a judgement without a number is a preference with a story attached, and the comparison has to be made once, in writing, at the time the component was chosen. The obligation afterwards is to state the consequence rather than bury it: what breaks, for whom, how often, and what would make the component worth replacing. The common failure is to record the delay as if recording it were the decision, which leaves the cost of being wrong unmeasured and the case for revisiting unmade.

answer.exemplar: A date dispute is settled by something neither side owns: the length of the chain of dependent work that remains, read against whatever date is fixed from outside the team. Written down, the argument stops being about confidence and becomes about two numbers that can both be checked, and a stakeholder who disagrees can point at a specific link in the chain rather than at a person. Confidence cannot settle it because every party is confident, and the most confident voice is not the best informed one. The common failure is to resolve it by status, meeting or vote, each of which replaces a fact with a preference; a vote cannot shorten a chain, and choosing the later date concedes the point without establishing that it is achievable.
